G2 is not covered by any existing document, and the code has no regeneration declaration either. I searched the plugin source for "regenerat" and found no match. I read the specs and `commands.py` only, and did not read the tests or the code in `checks.py` and `routing.py`.

ARTIFACT gap_finding: No spec or code holds a regeneration declaration. In `plugins/temperspec-tgraph/docs/specs/repository-commands.spec.md`, RCM-B1 to B9 and RCM-AC1 to AC9 cover verification commands only. The spec's Purpose calls `tempergraph.commands.json` the file declaring "which commands a run may use to verify its work". It has no inputs per command, no regeneration key and no changed-input trigger. Only RCM-B6 to B8 govern what prepare writes: a Python repository gets a fixed six-command list, a repository that is not Python gets nothing, and an existing file is left alone, so prepare invents no regenerations today. Engine side, CHK-B11 (`check-contract-and-command-runs.spec.md` line 38) defines the file as `{"commands": ["<prefix>", …]}`, read for a step or check listing `@repository`, with a missing or malformed file declaring none. A command that is not declared gets `CommandRefusal` with reason `not declared`, and shell metacharacters, parent paths and absolute paths are refused too. CHK-B12 (line 44) runs a resolved command with a list argv, no shell, stdin closed, a time limit and a scrubbed `CommandRun`. SEC-B5 (`security.spec.md` line 11) requires argv as a list with no shell. The code in `engine/src/tempergraph/run/commands.py` matches this: `REPO_FILE` (line 31), `repository_commands` (lines 41-52, which accepts only `schema_version == 1` with a `commands` list), `resolve_command` (line 98) and `run_command` (line 141). The package reads the file in `workflow/temperspec/checks.py` (1215-1216) and `routing.py` (472), with a comment at `__init__.py` 96. Gap: a regeneration entry needs a new key or file, a per-entry input list, and either a CHK-B11 extension or a package-level reader. The audit specs AUD-B17 to B19 read the file as commands and would be affected. This is not an existing-behaviour gap.
